text.p: ZAGREB, Nov 11 (Zagreb) - Following are the main stories in Croatian dailies on Monday.
- Many Serbs in the last rebel enclave of East Slavonia are interested in government health security programme despite reluctance to accept full Zagreb rule.
- Famous BBC TV-repoter Martin Bell believes Croat general Tihomir Blaskic endicted and held by Hague war crimes tribunal is an honourable man. Bell had recently testified in front of that court.

- Parliamnet will this week discuss draft law on privatisation of former socialist institutions' property. The law proposes the assets should first go to the state and be distributed to various parties after a one-year period.
- Almost a half of Croatians living in Germany are regeistered as Yugoslav citizens. Croatia estimates 450,000 of its people live in Germany, while German statistics speak of 185,122 Croatians.

- Privatisation law set no limits on a number of companies where a single person could buy shares at discount prices. It only said maximum 20,000 Geman marks worth cheaper shares could be bought in each company, says Jaksa Gabric, recently charged with malpractises by the ruling HDZ party.
- Ministry of tourism expects 1997 season to yield $2.5 million profit and 20 percent more tourists.

- Environmentalists in Istria strongly oppose building of the Plomin 2 power-plant, but investors hope to calm them down by promissing to spend a 100 million German marks on marinas, a new port, roads, green-houses and tourist resorts. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
